info.name: Zimal Store — Seller Onboarding (Phase 8a: Document Expiry & Re-KYC)
info.description:
Phase 8a manual test — expiring KYC documents and the re-KYC flow.

BEFORE YOU START
1) php artisan migrate
2) keep `php artisan queue:work` running (notifications + audit are queued)
3) you need an APPROVED store whose owner = {{seller_email}}
4) you need an admin ({{admin_email}}) who is NOT that store's owner —
   C12: nobody reviews their own documents
5) have a PDF or JPG on hand to upload as the 'new' document

THE POINT OF THIS PHASE
Before it, a CNIC was only checked once — on the day the application was
approved. It could expire years later and nobody would know. Now the
expiry DATES live in their own plain columns on seller_profiles (the AI
extract itself is encrypted and cannot be queried), a nightly command
finds them, and the seller can upload a replacement.

WHAT EXPIRY DOES (P8-2): the store stays OPEN and keeps selling. Only
PAYOUTS stop. Earning is allowed, withdrawing is not, until a fresh
document is approved.

TWO SEPARATE FACTS (P8-3): bank_verification_status answers 'is this bank
account proven theirs?'. kyc_status answers 'is their identity still
valid?'. Two questions, two columns — watch `payout_ready` in folder 1a,
it needs BOTH.

ORDER: 0 (tokens) -> 1 (seller uploads) -> 2 (admin approves)
       -> 3 (rejection path) -> 4 (the nightly sweep) -> 5 (errors).

request.description: The store OWNER's account — the same customer account that was approved as a seller.
accessible_panels should include 'seller'.

item.name: 1a. My store — look at the kyc block

request.description:
Read `data.kyc` and `data.payout_ready`.

kyc.status      valid | expiring_soon | expired
kyc.expires_on  the SOONEST of the CNIC and licence dates
kyc.blocks_payout   true only when expired
payout_ready    needs BOTH the bank verified AND kyc not expired (P8-3)

If expires_on is null, this store has no recorded date — that is NOT
expired, it just means nothing is known (C27). Most stores look like
this while AI verification is off.

The seller's own view. Deliberately does NOT include the AI extract —
reading your own CNIC number back at you serves no purpose — and never
the private file path (D7).

item.name: 1c. Upload a replacement CNIC (front) — saves renewal_id

request.description:
form-data:
  document_type = cnic_front | cnic_back | business_license
  file          = PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

ORDER OF CHECKS (this is the whole design):
  1. store open + caller is the OWNER   -> 403 if not
  2. no other pending renewal of this type -> 409 if there is
  3. rate limit (20/hour)                -> 429 if over
  4. ONLY THEN the AI reads the file
  5. only then is the file written to disk
Every one of 1-3 happens BEFORE the billable AI call, and a rejected
file is never stored.

With AI OFF (the default) ai_status comes back 'skipped' and
expires_on is null — the admin then reads the date off the document
by eye.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

item.name: 1d. My renewals — now one is pending

request.description:
status should be 'pending'. Nothing has changed on the store yet —
the date only moves when an admin approves (P8-4).

Oldest first on purpose: a seller whose payouts are frozen should not
sit behind someone who uploaded this morning.

The admin view adds what the seller's view hides: ai_fields (what the
AI read), ai_concerns, and store.payouts_on_hold — which tells the
reviewer this one is holding up someone's money.

Streams the file from the PRIVATE disk. The download name is OURS
('renewal-12-cnic_front.pdf'), never the seller's own file name — C14,
nothing user-controlled goes into a Content-Disposition header.

On approve, inside ONE transaction:
  - the renewal row becomes 'approved'
  - the extracted date is copied onto seller_profiles (cnic_expires_at
    or licence_expires_at)
  - kyc_status is recomputed from the new dates
  - kyc_notified_at is cleared, so the NEXT expiry cycle can warn
    again instead of staying silent (C29)

The row is locked FOR UPDATE, so two admins clicking at once means the
second one waits and then gets a 409 (C13).

kyc.status should be back to 'valid' and payout_ready true (assuming
the bank was already verified).

Note what did NOT change: bank_verification_status. Expiry never
touched it, so there was nothing to restore — that is exactly why it
is a separate column (P8-3).
Allowed because nothing is pending now — the previous one was reviewed.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

request.description:
A reason is REQUIRED on reject — a rejection the seller cannot act on
is useless to them. The reason is emailed to them verbatim.
rejection_reason carries the admin's words.

A rejection is not a dead end — nothing is pending any more, so a
fresh upload of the same type is allowed.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

item.name: 4. The nightly expiry sweep
item.description:
This part is NOT an HTTP endpoint — it is the scheduled command.

TO TEST IT BY HAND:
  1) set a date in the past or near future directly in the DB:
       UPDATE seller_profiles SET cnic_expires_at = '2026-10-05',
              kyc_status = 'valid', kyc_notified_at = NULL WHERE id = <id>;
  2) php artisan seller:check-document-expiry
  3) run 4a below and watch kyc.status move

WHAT TO CHECK
  - a store with BOTH dates NULL is never touched (C27). This is the one
    that matters: if NULL were read as expired, every existing seller's
    payouts would freeze the day AI verification is switched on.
  - running the command twice in a row sends only ONE email. It reports a
    state CHANGE, not a condition (C29) — that is what kyc_notified_at is
    for. Without it the same seller would be emailed every morning for
    thirty days.
  - within 30 days -> expiring_soon (store open, payouts still fine)
  - past the date  -> expired (store STILL open, payouts held)

In production it runs daily at 03:00, withoutOverlapping.

request.description:
tax_certificate has no expiry, and bank_statement has its own proof
flow (P6-2). Neither can be renewed here.

item.name: E2. Two pending of the same type -> 409

request.description:
Run this straight after 3d (which left a business_license pending).
A second one would leave the admin guessing which is current.

Note this 409 arrives WITHOUT an AI call — the pending check runs
first, so a duplicate upload costs nothing.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

request.description:
OPTIONAL — needs {{manager_token}} (a manager or staff member of the
same store, from the Phase 7 collection).

A renewal replaces the OWNER'S OWN identity document. A manager runs
the shop; someone else's CNIC is not theirs to replace.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

item.name: E4. Review the same renewal twice -> 409

request.description: Run this twice in a row. The second one is refused.
reason is required_if:decision,reject.

item.name: E7. An admin reviewing their OWN store -> 403

request.description:
Only reproducible if {{admin_email}} also owns the store the renewal
belongs to. C12 — segregation of duties: a super admin is also an
ordinary user who may run a shop, and never reviews their own papers.

item.name: E8. A customer hits the admin queue -> 403

request.description:
20 uploads per hour, per USER (not per IP — everyone here is logged
in, and an IP key would punish a whole office behind one connection).

TO SEE IT: hit Send about 21 times. The first is a 201, the next ones
are 409s (one pending per type) — they still count — and then 429.

Why this exists at all: each upload is a billable AI call made BEFORE
the file is stored, so even a rejected upload costs money. The
throttle sits on the route, ahead of the controller, so a blocked
request never reaches the AI.

formdata.description: The replacement document — PDF / JPG / PNG, max 10 MB

exec: pm.test("429 once the hourly limit is hit", () => pm.expect([201,409,429]).to.include(pm.response.code));
